You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC

1. Parse the independent instance, grid, attempt/demo caps, counters, and allowed actions. On every puzzle turn, including demo requests, reply only with exactly one permitted action JSON object; do not add analysis, commentary, or tool calls. Treat boundary lines as dividers, not automatic instructions to copy every region: identify the specific source object/pattern and the exact destinations changed in demos. For sparse colored diagonals that become a full repeating grid, test whether each diagonal encodes one residue of a periodic color sequence: index cells by `column - row` modulo the candidate period, read the marker colors at those residues, then verify the same mapping at multiple positions and across demos before filling. Check the diagonal direction and phase explicitly; do not infer a general rule from a coincidental overlap or merely replace apparent gaps.
3. When multiple rules fit, request a demo that distinguishes them, especially before the first guess or after a wrong submission. Choose what to disambiguate explicitly (e.g. copy source into adjacent panel vs all panels, reflect vs translate, or replicate across a divider vs only fill the displayed repeat). A wrong result refutes that output: compare it cell-by-cell with the proposed rule and demos, revise the hypothesis, and request another discriminating demo rather than repeating speculative variants. A demo's matching dimensions/colors alone is not sufficient; verify its exact transformation signature and which regions remain unchanged. Treat the demo as evidence about the transformation, not as a template for color substitution: derive the rule from aligned input/output cells, including background and all marker colors, and check whether the demonstrated relation actually applies to the test before constructing an output.

# test grid panels 4x4 with vertical/horiz separators; marker at panel coordinates
# Demo indicates color 2 marker at panel row0 col1? Demo panels are 3x3 internal. Source marker in r0,c1 and r4,c1; output fills entire column panel c1 color2 across rows 0,1,3,4. Plus color3 markers at panel(2,0),(2,4) and output row 2 fills all panels with color3 except c1 =6. Rule likely markers indicate line propagation: replicate color 2 column vertically; color 3 row horizontally, intersections blend to 6. In test panels 4x4, marker 2 at (panel-row1,col0 local2) and (panel-row1,col5 local2), so fill entire panel row1 across? Wait rows separated at 4,9,... panel 4x4. 2 markers in panel row1 col0 and col5? coordinates (6,2), (6,22): same panel row band, same local row, different panel columns. Demo 2 markers at row0 and row4, same panel col1, local row1. Output fills panel column1 across all panel rows. Thus markers define same panel column, replicate column. Test 2 marks at (panel row1, columns0 and5), defines horizontal relation? 3 markers at panel row0,col2 local row1,col2; panel row4,col2 local row1,col2. Thus defines panel column2 fill? In demo 3 row markers panels row2 col0 and col3 local row1; output fills entire panel row2 in all columns. So opposite marker arrangement creates row fill. Test 3 at panel row0,col2 and row4,col2, same panel column, thus fill that panel column all panel rows, color 3. 2 markers same panel row across cols, fill entire panel row color2. Intersections potentially color based? demo 3 row has intersection with 2 col, output intersection 6 (new color maybe 2+3). Do so: 2 panel row band index1 across all panels color2, 3 panel col index2 all panels color3; intersection 6. Preserve separators. panel 4x4, interiors indices rows bands [0..3], [5..8] etc; cols likewise. fill regions; at intersection row band1 & col band2 ->6.
rows=[]
for r in range(28):
 row=[]

  if r%5==4 or c%5==4: v=8
  else:
   pr=r//5; pc=c//5
   if pr==1 and pc==2: v=6
   elif pr==1: v=2
   elif pc==2: v=3
   else: v=0
  row.append(v)
 rows.append(row)
print('{"action":"submit","grid":'+str(rows).replace(' ','')+'}')
